findings.title: Fallback locale files are not loaded on the translation path
findings.body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale for the active locale, and the new ensure_loaded! helper is never invoked from translate, with_locale, or reload. Fallback YAML is loaded only from ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, and any I18n.with_locale block therefore resolve fallbacks against unloaded site-default and :en files, so missing keys do not fall back to translations that exist on disk. No-argument lookups then freeze that miss in the LRU cache (key is only key+locale+backend), so a later load of the fallback locale still returns the wrong result until restart.

findings.title: Translation cache ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" and does not include SiteSetting.default_locale or the fallback list. FallbackLocaleList recomputes the chain on every lookup, but a cache hit never reaches the backend. After an admin changes the site default locale, strings that were filled from the old fallback stay pinned to the previous language for that user locale until the entry is evicted or the process reloads.

findings.title: Custom fallback list drops parent-locale fallbacks
findings.body: Production previously set config.i18n.fallbacks = true, which used I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and walked parent tags (zh_TW -> zh -> default locale). FallbackLocaleList#[] now returns only [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]. Regional locales no longer fall back to their language root, so a missing zh_TW key will not use an existing zh translation and will jump straight to the site default or English. The same method also calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym with no guard; if that setting is nil or SiteSetting cannot be read (boot, asset precompile, DB outage), every I18n lookup raises instead of translating.
